sources.subject: Current proof-session, obsolete/detached, replay, session and bench behavior
supports: session stores transformations and prover attempts
attempt records complete prover identity and resource/result information
obsolete attempts were run on earlier tasks and require replay
detached attempts have no current task but are retained and reusable
replay reruns stored attempts and compares current outcomes with stored outcomes

sources.subject: Current reload and old/new session merge semantics
supports: current files are reparsed on reload
theories match by exact name
goals match by exact name then shape
matched changed tasks retain attempts as obsolete
unmatched old nodes remain without current tasks
old transformations are reapplied and subgoals recursively matched
shape matching can be disabled

sources.subject: Durable session/runtime reconstruction boundary
supports: load_session initializes tasks to None
merge_files associates old session structure with reconstructed files
proof attempts and transformations are graftable session records
change_prover is an explicit session operation

sources.subject: why3session.xml durable fields
supports: session XML stores prover/version/limits
goal records include name/checksum/shape
proof records include obsolete and result state
transformation records include names/arguments

sources.subject: Prover upgrade policy
supports: old sessions retain old prover identity
keep/remove/upgrade/copy policies
new-version upgraded/copied attempts are obsolete and require replay
interactive proof scripts may be reused or duplicated

sources.subject: Historical evolution of session matching and replay
supports: 0.70 introduced batch session replay
0.71 introduced goal-shape pairing and prover-version obsolescence
0.72 added multiple prover versions and prover upgrade
0.73 retained backward session readability and obsolete-only replay
0.84 split shapes/checksums into a sidecar useful for tracking obsolete goals but not required for replay
1.7.0 expanded session manipulation and shape-ignore support

sources.subject: Proof-session preservation rationale and reported experience

identity.title: Preserving User Proofs Across Specification Changes

supports: specification/code changes invalidate related proof obligations while old proof work may remain reusable
Why3 implements session maintenance across changing verification conditions
authors report use on more than one hundred verified programs and during tool/library evolution
authors identify prover upgrades as another session-maintenance use case

derived_judgments: Use stronger identity for current acceptance than for repair/salvage matching.
Heuristic old/new matching may select work to replay but must not make stale results current.
Persist reconstructible workflow and provenance rather than requiring durability of live RPC objects.
Retain unmatched expensive work as detached salvage without counting it as coverage or allowing it to block fresh work.
Treat native publication/effect reconciliation as a separate protocol from proof-session durability.
